knowledge_point.title: Integrating Products Containing Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x^{3}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=18 x^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{18}\text{d}u=x^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5 x^{2} \sec^{2}{\left(6 x^{3} \right)}\,\text{d}x & =\int 5 \sec^{2}{\left(6 x^{3} \right)}\cdot x^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{18}\right)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{18}\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5 \tan{\left(u \right)}}{18}+C \\  & =\frac{5 \tan{\left(6 x^{3} \right)}}{18}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=x^{2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $\frac{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}$ | $\sqrt{\pi /2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\frac{\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\pi}}{2}} 11 x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\text{d}x & =\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\pi}}{2}} 11 \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 11 \cos{\left(u \right)}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{11 \sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\big|_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\left(\sin{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}-\left(\sin{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \right)}\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{11}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
If we let $u=x^{2},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi /3$ |

Using the above, we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{3}} 11 x \tan{\left(x^{2} \right)} \sec{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\text{d}x & =\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{3}} 11 \tan{\left(x^{2} \right)} \sec{\left(x^{2} \right)}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \tan{\left(u \right)} \sec{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{11 \sec{\left(u \right)}}{2}\big|_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\left(\sec{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \right)}-\left(\sec{\left(\left(0\right) \right)}\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\left(2-\left(1\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
